topics.statusLabel: 未经教师书面许可默认禁止（采纳规范学院）
topics.summary: Under Columbia University's decentralized academic governance, coursework policies vary by school: schools adhering to CSSI Standards & Discipline (§C.3) treat unauthorized AI assistance as academic dishonesty requiring instructor written permission; Columbia Law School establishes a default permitting defined research and writing support unless the instructor alters it in writing (§8, §Default); and Columbia Business School requires following syllabus-designated assignment modes.
topics.scope: Students across Columbia University schools (governed by individual school Dean adoption, Law School defaults, or school honor codes)
actions: Check your school-specific policy and course syllabus to determine whether AI is permitted for coursework, and obtain written instructor permission where required by school policy.
Exercise independent critical thinking and verify all AI-generated references, arguments, and citations before incorporation.
Do not assume permissions are uniform across all schools; adhere to specific syllabus instructions and school rules.

topics.summary: Under both CSSI Standards & Discipline and Columbia Law School Policy (§9.1), generative AI is strictly prohibited on examinations unless advance written permission is granted by the instructor in the syllabus and/or examination instructions. actions: Verify whether advance written authorization for AI use exists on the syllabus or exam cover sheet.
Produce every word of your exam answers independently without unauthorized AI assistance.
Never input exam questions, prompts, or fact patterns into any AI tool (strictly prohibited at Law School).

At CUIMC, Workspace Gemini/Gemini Notebook lack a HIPAA BAA and must not receive Sensitive Data; FERPA records can contain identifying/health elements requiring the stricter Sensitive Data treatment. Use only CUIT-vetted secure environments or CUIMC HIPAA-approved platforms for protected clinical or confidential research data.
Adhere to the 'Minimum Necessary' principle and de-identify data whenever possible.

topics.summary: Under central Provost policy, researchers must not enter confidential research data, unpublished scholarly manuscripts, funding proposals, or research subject PII into public or unvetted AI tools, and using generative AI for peer review is strictly prohibited. Research analysis involving confidential or sensitive data must be conducted within CUIT-approved secure environments following IRB protocols, data use agreements, and sponsor requirements. Locally installed models require formal IT Risk Assessment.

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与纪律处分程序
additionalTopics.statusLabel: 院长纪律程序与检测器证据限制
additionalTopics.summary: Under Columbia University's Standards & Discipline (applicable to adhering schools at each Dean's discretion), unauthorized AI assistance is addressed through the Dean's Discipline process administered by CSSI. A report from an AI detection tool cannot be the sole piece of proof used to find a student responsible in a Dean’s Discipline case. Appeal timing under that process, subject to the recorded extension/final-notice qualifications, includes: 5 business days after receipt of the outcome letter, 5 business days for CSSI review, 2 business days from return for resubmission, and 10 business days from receipt for Dean review (with a 10 business day final notification qualifier from receipt). Under Columbia Law School default rules (§9.2, §11), submitted work must be student-composed, and submitting translated drafts of one's own non-English writing as original English work is prohibited by default (subject to written instructor alternatives).
additionalTopics.scope: Adhering schools under Dean's Discipline authority; Columbia Law School disciplinary referrals
actions: Submit only authentic student-composed work reflecting your independent intellectual judgment.
Note strict appeal deadlines (5 business days after receipt of outcome letter; 2 business days for resubmissions).
Rely on qualitative academic evidence rather than AI detector scores, which are inadmissible under CSSI policy.
